svg.title: Undercarriage Wear Thresholds
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-undercarriage-wear-thresholds; chapter number: 4; title: Undercarriage Wear Thresholds; subtitle: Measure component by component, never accept a seller's percentage; chart type: stacked_comparison; total range: 31% measured wear to a 60% pin and bush turn point; buckets: label: Measured Komatsu wear at 4,700 hours; low: 31; high: 31; notes: 1,010 of 3,200 points on a 2010 Komatsu excavator.; label: Price as needing undercarriage soon; low: 40; high: 50; notes: Wear accelerates past this band; not half its life left.; label: Pin and bush turn trigger; low: 60; high: 60; notes: Turn at 7,000 hours or 60% wear on the rails.; label: Remaining life on scored Komatsu; low: 69; high: 69; notes: Likely original undercarriage.; caption: Undercarriage replacement runs 12,000 to upwards of 70 grand, so pumped-tight tracks, cut links, and welded adjusters get checked before bidding.; assumptions note: Percentages are wear unless labeled remaining. Oil samples cost less than 10 dollars typical, less than 20 on the high side, with 24 to 48 hour turnaround; Carter recommends sampling every 250 hours.; note: Sources - C&C Equipment, Hunter Valley Tracks, Volvo Construction Equipment - North America, Shelly Eckert of Chevron via EquipmentWorld, and Carter Machinery.
